thread:
marta: Quick heads-up — aiming to publish py/ts SDK 1.8.0 in today's quiet window (14:00-17:00 PT). Main changes: remove legacy sync client, bump peer deps, add deprecation note for sync client in README + CHANGELOG.

sam: copying release checklist here. are we gating canary? :eyes:

marta: yes — canary cohort for 30m then stagger to full. publish-bot will run the canary tag. If sigs or wheels fail we abort.

jon: who is owning the release notes PR? need the deprecation text to be explicit about migration path. also confirm py wheel signing is on.

marta: tina has the release notes PR (#487). pinged her to add migration snippet. wheel signing: yes, sigs enabled on CI, but we had earlier flaky HSM timeouts — watch logs.

lee: quick ops question: what's the pinback policy if we need to yank? do we soft-pin older dist-tag or yank entirely?

sam: recommended flow: soft-pin by adding a dist-tag for the previous stable and set publish to fallback. only yank if integrity is compromised. Example: `npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.7.4 stable` then `npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk next` for canary fallback. For pip, `pip index versions redwood-sdk` and republish with twine retag if needed.

publish-bot: deploy check: all checks green for py and ts packages. canary run scheduled at 14:05 PT.

jon: add gating: if >1% of canary clients log runtime errors within 10m -> automatic hold. who will triage?

marta: ops oncall + devex (sam) will triage. rollback criteria: critical exceptions, signature mismatch, severe perf regressions (>2x p50). Otherwise prefer patch release.

tina: PR updated with migration snippet and example code: `from redwood import AsyncClient` -> `from redwood import Client` + tiny adapter. also added deprecation header in README.

lee: CI note — please ensure `GPG_KEY_ID` is set for the wheel signing job. last time it fell back to unsigned wheels and pypi rejected.

marta: verified with infra: GPG_KEY_ID present in release-runner. I re-ran signing job in staging earlier.

sam: one more thing — documentation site deploy will run after publish. keep an eye on docs redirect for sync-client entries. we should add a prominent banner for 2 weeks.

jon: on rollback ops: command snippets if we must revert quickly:
```
# npm fallback to previous stable
npm dist-tag add @redwood/sdk@1.7.4 stable
# remove canary tag
npm dist-tag rm @redwood/sdk next
# PyPI: republish previous wheel (if available) or set pinned artifact in internal index
twine upload --repository-url https://pypi.internal.example/ dist/redwood_sdk-1.7.4-py3-none-any.whl
```

marta: good. i'll open an incident room if we hit the hold criteria. For now proceed with canary at 14:05 PT. @tina, @sam please be online 14:00-15:00 for rapid triage.

tina: on it. linking release notes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/487

publish-bot: canary completed at 14:35 PT — 200 installs, no errors flagged. scheduling stagger to 3 cohorts at 14:50, 15:20, 15:50.

lee: watching package signing logs — all wheels signed and checksums match.

sam: docs banner deployed to staging. will roll to prod after cohort 2 if no issues.

marta: cohort 2 went OK. cohort 3 in progress. if all green we'll cut GA tag and publish release notes. thanks everyone. :rocket:
